question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $18$ modulo $48$ is the integer $0\le x<48$ such that

$$
x+18≡0\,(\text{mod}\,48).
$$

Now, notice that when we add our two numbers, we get a number that is *not* congruent to zero modulo $48:$

$$
\begin{aligned}34+18 & ≡52 & \,(\text{mod}\,48) \\  & ≡48+4 & \,(\text{mod}\,48) \\  & ≡4 & \,(\text{mod}\,48) \\  & ≢0 & \,(\text{mod}\,48)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude the following:

The integer $34$ $\text{is not}$ the additive inverse of $18$ modulo $48$ since $34+18≢0\,(\text{mod}\,48).$

$$
x+13≡0\,(\text{mod}\,37).
$$

Now, notice that when we add our two numbers, we get a number that is *not* congruent to zero modulo $37:$

$$
\begin{aligned}14+13 & ≡27 & \,(\text{mod}\,37) \\  & ≢0 & \,(\text{mod}\,37)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude the following:

The integer $14$ $\text{is not}$ the additive inverse of $13$ modulo $27$ since $14+13≢0\,(\text{mod}\,37).$
